title: Introduce sidecar aggregation proxy to isolate console hotpath
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Problem: The console backend experiences intermittent tail latency spikes driven by aggregation hotpaths: high-cardinality fanouts that traverse shared GraphQL resolvers and a single aggregator service. These spikes are hard to mitigate because requests with hot keys contend on shared caches and CPU, causing noisy neighbor effects for other routes.

Goal: Reduce 95th/99th percentile tail latency for console API routes by isolating aggregation hot paths into a lightweight sidecar proxy layer. The sidecar should: 1) own per-route small LRU caches, 2) coalesce duplicate in-flight fetches per-key, and 3) forward cold misses to the existing aggregation pipeline. We must avoid large refactors in the runtime and keep the change deployable to Dedicated and Private installs with feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for /console/aggregate endpoints reduced by >= 30% in staging (synthetic traffic) compared to baseline
No increase in error rate or significant CPU cost for non-isolated routes (<5% change)
Sidecar deployed behind a feature flag and validated in Canary for < 1% of production traffic before full rollout
Unit and integration tests cover cache eviction, in-flight coalescing, and fallback paths
Design doc reviewed and approved by platform reliability and API teams (link in links)
technical_notes: Sidecar will be implemented as a thin HTTP/GRPC proxy in Go to match existing console stack and minimize latency overhead
Local caches are sharded per-process with size tuned per-route; default LRU size 1024 keys, configurable via Console routing config
In-flight coalescing uses singleflight-like mechanism per-key to prevent duplicate upstream fanouts
Telemetry: emit per-request metric for cache hit/miss, coalesced_count, and upstream_fallback_latency to Console observability
Compatibility: sidecar must pass through tracing headers (traceparent/b3) and propagate auth tokens unchanged
implementation_plan: Phase 1 - Spike (1 week): implement prototype sidecar locally, implement LRU + singleflight, run synthetic benchmark vs baseline
Phase 2 - Integration (2 weeks): add routing config, telemetry, and graceful fallback to existing aggregator; add unit/integration tests
Phase 3 - Canary (1 week): rollout 1% traffic in staging and then production behind feature flag; monitor metrics and adjust cache sizes
Phase 4 - Rollout (1 week): incrementally increase traffic to 25%/50%/100% with automated abort conditions based on latency/error thresholds
Phase 5 - Post-mortem & cleanup (1 week): remove temporary instrumentation, publish runbook and update architecture diagram
rollout_plan: Deploy sidecar as an additional container in Console backend pods (host-network disabled)
Enable via Console config flag: console.routes.<route>.sidecar_enabled = true
Canary gating: monitor 95th/99th latency, error rate, and coalesced_count; automated rollback if >20% latency regression for 10 minutes
Add smoke checks to CI to ensure sidecar starts and responds to healthcheck endpoints
Coordinate with infra for Dedicated/Private packaging and update helm chart values
risks: Sidecar adds another moving part; if buggy, could increase request latency — mitigated by default-disabled feature flag and canary gating
Incorrect cache sizing could skew results or cause memory pressure — mitigated by conservative defaults and per-route knobs
Observability gaps if tracing or metrics not propagated — will add tests to assert header propagation and metric emission
Deployment complexity for Private customers — will prepare an upgrade doc and compatibility checklist
